non_claims: The C-glycosylation position (6-C versus 8-C) is not claimed; the published intensity-ratio criteria for it depend on collision energy and instrument
Sugar identity (hexose versus pentose), unit counts and the aglycone formula come from the chosen hypothesis and are not claimed

The aglycone skeleton rests on the precondition's flavonoid formula list, which isobaric non-flavonoid aglycones can share (for example aloe-emodin anthrone, C15H12O4, in aloin); anthrone C-glycosides are listed as a competitor

notes: Protonated mono-C-glycosyl flavonoids give the 0,2X+ and aglycone+C (0,1X+) ions of the C-sugar while the even and radical aglycone ions stay weak; water-loss ions dominate at low collision energy.

competitors.note: Flavonoid O-glycosides share compositions with C-glycosides (apigenin 7-O-glucoside and vitexin are both C21H20O10) and lose whole sugars to a strong Y0.
Anthrone C-glycosides (aloin C21H22O9, 10-hydroxyaloin C21H22O10) have the compositions of C15H12O4 and C15H12O5 hexoside hypotheses, so their C-glucose cross-ring targets coincide with x02 and agc.

terms.note: 0,2X+ of the C-sugar (water loss with ring cleavage): Hex loses C4H8O4 (120), Pen loses C3H6O3 (90)
Aglycone + C ion [aglycone+C+H]+ (0,1X+, alpha cleavage of the C-sugar), a loss of C5H10O5 (150) for Hex or C4H8O4 (120) for Pen
Y0 [aglycone+H]+, a few percent for flavone C-glucosides but dominant for O-glycosides
Radical Y0 [aglycone]+., listed only for the C-6-glucosides and below their 0,1X+ and 0,2X+ ions
